categories.name: Market days
categories.description: Dates, weather and what to expect.

posts.title: Autumn workshop dates
posts.excerpt: Indigo in October, spoon carving in November, small baskets in December.
posts.content:
Each workshop takes eight people and starts at 11:00 by the shrine hall. Book a place by email the week before.

Wear clothes you do not mind staining. Indigo washes off hands in a day, but never off a white shirt.

posts.title: Meet our new basket weaver
posts.excerpt: She learned from her grandfather and now splits her own bamboo from the hill behind the shrine.
posts.content:
The bamboo is cut in winter, when the stalks hold the least water. She dries it for months before weaving.

Her market baskets take three days each. Bring an old one and she will tell you how to make it last.

posts.title: Why the market opens at nine
posts.excerpt: Makers arrive at seven. Here is what happens in those two quiet hours.
posts.content:
Awnings go up, pots come out of straw and neighbours swap change. Most makers have known each other for years.

It is also when they buy from each other. Some of the best bowls are gone before the gate opens.
